READING

**The pivotal asymmetry**

Both courses share one feature: if the renewal is lodged with an undertaking rather than a certificate, the precedents (Cadgarth 2024, Nant Elwy 2025) make a six-year term the expected outcome, not fifteen. A six-year renewal from May 2028 expires May 2034. The loan runs to 2039. The bank's June 2026 letter is explicit: a licence term shorter than the loan puts the facility under review. For a two-person operation with a single £480,000 facility and a single 240 kW turbine, "under review" is not a nuisance – it is an existential threat.

PENNYQUAY locks in that six-year outcome and therefore almost certainly triggers the bank clause. LINTHAUGH is the only course that contains a path to fifteen years, because only a fish-pass compliance certificate supports the full term and only the derogation route can deliver one before the 2027-05-31 deadline.

---

**Assessing the derogation probability**

The raw grant rate was 4/11 in 2025. That looks unfavourable, but the stated reason for every refusal is decisive: each refused scheme had no dated regulatory driver. Blaenclydach's driver is as hard-dated as it gets – a statutory renewal deadline of 2027-05-31 tied to the 2028-05-31 licence expiry, with the twelve-month lodgement rule removing any discretion. The Board's own published reasoning means Blaenclydach is categorically unlike the refused schemes. The effective probability of grant is substantially above 4/11; even conservatively, call it 60–70%.

---

**Working through the deposit risk**

The £46,000 deposit is non-returnable after 2026-12-01. In a refusal scenario (decided 2027-01-25), it is lost. That is a real cost. But the deposit is not paid until 2026-12-01, which is after the derogation is lodged (2026-10-19) and before the decision (2027-01-25). The sequence means the deposit is committed while the outcome is unknown. However, the problem as stated treats the deposit as integral to Course LINTHAUGH; Rhoswen pays it as part of securing the February slot simultaneously with lodging the derogation. That is the premise I work from.

---

**Worst-case LINTHAUGH vs PENNYQUAY**

If the derogation is refused on 2027-01-25:
- The deadline of 2027-05-31 is exactly 18 weeks away (126 days). The undertaking route can still be filed in time.
- The July slot can be booked – Vossbeck confirms it by 2027-04-30, which is reachable after a January refusal.
- The screen and bearing set go in during the July window (same as PENNYQUAY).
- The result is the same six-year renewal and the same bank problem.
- The additional wasted cost is £9,000 (application) + £46,000 (deposit) = £55,000.

So the worst case for LINTHAUGH is: PENNYQUAY outcome plus £55,000 extra cost. The best case for LINTHAUGH is: no bank problem, fifteen-year licence, business secured through 2043, loan covered to 2039.

---

**Comparing the cost structures**

| Item | LINTHAUGH (granted) | LINTHAUGH (refused) | PENNYQUAY |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|-----------|
| Derogation fee | £9,000 | £9,000 | – |
| Deposit at risk | £46,000 | £46,000 lost | – |
| Export loss | £19,152 (168 MWh × 11.4p) | £8,436 (July) | £8,436 (July) |
| Licence term | 15 years → 2043 | 6 years → 2034 | 6 years → 2034 |
| Bank trigger | No | Yes | Yes |

Even in the granted scenario, the incremental cost over PENNYQUAY is roughly £65,700. That is the price of the option to avoid a bank review on a £480,000 loan. For a small hydro with no alternative asset base, the value of that option overwhelms the option's cost.

---

**The undertaking route is not a safe fallback – it is the failure mode**

PENNYQUAY presents the undertaking path as acceptable because the Board has accepted undertakings before. That is true. What the problem also tells us is that both schemes that used that route got six years, not fifteen, and that Rhoswen's own bank has already written to say a term short of the loan term triggers a review. Filing with an undertaking is not a conservative option; it is a route that, on present evidence, reliably produces the one outcome Blaenclydach cannot afford.

---

**The dated regulatory driver point again – and why it matters to the decision**

The derogation application would cite: (a) the 2028-05-31 licence expiry; (b) the statutory twelve-month lodgement rule producing a hard 2027-05-31 deadline; (c) the compliance certificate requirement making an out-of-season screen installation the only way to meet it. That is a textbook dated regulatory driver. The Rivers Board's own published refusal rationale means accepting this application is entirely consistent with their practice; refusing it would contradict their stated grounds. The probability of refusal is materially lower than the raw 7/11.

---

**Conclusion**

LINTHAUGH is the only course that offers a realistic path to a fifteen-year renewal. PENNYQUAY virtually guarantees six years, virtually guarantees the bank clause, and cannot be rescued by subsequent good performance because the certificate will come too late to change the renewal term. The costs of LINTHAUGH are real but proportionate. The dated regulatory driver makes the derogation application genuinely strong. The fallback in a refusal is uncomfortable but survivable. The fallback in PENNYQUAY is the bank clause, which may not be.

---

CALL
  LINTHAUGH

GROUNDS
  PENNYQUAY's undertaking route reliably produces a six-year licence term that falls five years short of the 2039 loan maturity and so virtually guarantees the bank-review trigger, whereas LINTHAUGH's derogation application rests on a hard-dated statutory driver that the Rivers Board's own published refusals confirm is the decisive positive factor, making the extra costs of the February route a proportionate price for the only realistic path to a fifteen-year renewal that keeps the loan facility secure.
